x_to_y: This edge represents the idea that changes in \(x\) cause changes in \(y\), i.e., shifting \(x\) (through policy, prices, technology, or an intervention) would move the outcome \(y\) holding other relevant factors fixed. The main risks to a valid causal estimate are omitted confounders that affect both \(x\) and \(y\), reverse causality if \(y\) also influences \(x\), and measurement error in \(x\) that can attenuate or distort the estimated effect. Next, a researcher should map and justify the adjustment set implied by the DAG, assess pre-trends/placebo outcomes if using quasi-experimental variation, and probe sensitivity to alternative controls or instruments that shift \(x\) without directly affecting \(y\).
